2º de Bachillerato · Inglés II

The passive, impersonal passive and causative

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

En español decimos «Se dice que el castillo está encantado». ¿Cómo se dice en inglés si no existe el «se»?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Con una pasiva impersonal o una pasiva personal. It is said that the castle is haunted, o mejor, The castle is said to be haunted. Si el rumor habla del pasado: The castle is said to have been built in the 12th century. El inglés usa la voz pasiva mucho más que el español, sobre todo en noticias, ciencia y textos formales, justo los que aparecen en la PAU.

2

Aprende12 apartados

Para empezar: The painting that was stolen twice

In August 1911, the Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre. At first, nobody noticed it was missing: the guards thought it was being photographed. The poet Guillaume Apollinaire was arrested, and even Pablo Picasso was questioned by the police. Neither of them had anything to do with it.

The thief, an Italian decorator called Vincenzo Peruggia, is believed to have hidden inside a cupboard overnight. He is said to have walked out of the museum with the painting under his coat. The Mona Lisa was kept in his flat in Paris for two years before he tried to sell it in Florence, where he was caught.

Today the painting is protected by bulletproof glass and is visited by around ten million people a year. It has been attacked several times since then: in 2022 a visitor had a cake thrown at the glass. Fortunately, the painting wasn't damaged.

En la noticia casi todos los verbos están en voz pasiva: lo importante es el cuadro, no quién hizo cada cosa. Este tema enseña a usarla con la soltura de un texto periodístico.

4.1 Por qué se usa la voz pasiva

En la voz activa el sujeto hace la acción: Peruggia stole the Mona Lisa. En la voz pasiva el sujeto la recibe: The Mona Lisa was stolen (by Peruggia). El objeto de la activa pasa a sujeto, el verbo se construye con be + participio y el sujeto de la activa, si aparece, va con by.

La pasiva se usa cuando interesa más la acción o el objeto que quien la realiza: cuando el agente es desconocido (My bike has been stolen), obvio (He was arrested, por la policía), poco importante (English is spoken here) o cuando queremos un tono impersonal y objetivo (Mistakes were made).

El agente con by solo se incluye si aporta información nueva o importante: Guernica was painted by Picasso. Frases como *The thief was arrested by the police o *by someone suenan redundantes.

La pasiva también ayuda a organizar la información: en inglés, lo conocido suele ir al principio y lo nuevo al final. This bridge is one of the oldest in Europe. It was built by the Romans. Así el texto fluye mejor.

Es muy frecuente en noticias, textos científicos, instrucciones, informes y normas, por lo que aparece constantemente en los textos de comprensión de la PAU.

4.2 La pasiva en todos los tiempos

La regla es siempre la misma: el verbo be se pone en el tiempo de la frase activa y se añade el participio del verbo principal.

TiempoActivaPasiva
present simpleThey make cars here.Cars are made here.
present continuousThey are repairing the road.The road is being repaired.
past simpleThey built it in 1900.It was built in 1900.
past continuousThey were interviewing him.He was being interviewed.
present perfectThey have sold the house.The house has been sold.
past perfectThey had cancelled the flight.The flight had been cancelled.
future (will)They will announce it.It will be announced.
be going toThey are going to close it.It is going to be closed.
future perfectThey will have finished it.It will have been finished.

Las formas pasivas de los tiempos perfectos continuos (*has been being built) existen en teoría, pero casi no se usan: se prefiere el present perfect simple o el continuo de otra manera (The road has been under construction for months).

Para transformar una frase, sigue tres pasos: identifica el objeto (será el nuevo sujeto), conserva el tiempo de la activa en be y decide si el agente es necesario.

4.3 Pasiva con modales, infinitivos y gerundios

Con modales la pasiva es modal + be + participio en presente y modal + have been + participio en pasado: This form must be signed. The problem could have been avoided. Phones should be switched off.

El infinitivo pasivo (to be done) aparece detrás de verbos como want, need, expect, hope, would like y de adjetivos: I want to be informed. The windows need to be cleaned. This is likely to be decided tomorrow. En pasado: to have been done: She was lucky to have been chosen.

El gerundio pasivo (being done) aparece detrás de verbos y preposiciones que llevan -ing: I hate being interrupted. He's afraid of being criticised. She left without being seen. En pasado: having been done: Having been warned, they stayed indoors.

Estas formas son típicas de un registro avanzado y de los ensayos: Young people want to be listened to. Nobody likes being told what to do. More measures need to be taken. Fíjate en que la preposición se mantiene al final (listened to).

4.4 Verbos con dos objetos

Verbos como give, send, offer, show, tell, lend, award, promise, teach tienen dos objetos: uno indirecto (la persona) y otro directo (la cosa). They gave Ana a prize. Cualquiera de los dos puede ser sujeto de la pasiva:

Ana was given a prize (lo más frecuente en inglés: la persona como sujeto). A prize was given to Ana (si queremos destacar la cosa; la persona va con to).

Esta construcción es muy distinta del español, que no puede decir *«Ana fue dada un premio». Por eso es una pregunta habitual de examen: I was told that the exam had been cancelled. We were shown the new laboratory. She has been offered a job in Berlin.

Algunos verbos no admiten a la persona como sujeto porque la persona va siempre con preposición en la activa: explain, describe, suggest, propose, announce, report. Se dice The rules were explained to us, no *We were explained the rules. Es un error típico de hispanohablantes.

4.5 Verbos con preposición, phrasal verbs y la pasiva con get

Cuando el verbo va con una preposición o es un phrasal verb, la partícula se queda pegada al verbo en la pasiva y suele quedar al final: Someone is looking after the children → The children are being looked after. They turned down my application → My application was turned down. Everybody laughed at him → He was laughed at.

Otros ejemplos frecuentes: The meeting has been called off. The problem must be dealt with immediately. This issue will be looked into. The patient was operated on yesterday.

En el registro informal, get + participio sustituye a be para acciones que ocurren de forma inesperada o negativa: My phone got stolen. He got injured in the match. They got married last year. Don't get caught! No se usa con verbos de estado (*The house got owned) ni en textos formales.

Expresiones fijas con get: get dressed, get lost, get hurt, get fired, get paid, get involved, get promoted. Son muy útiles en la expresión oral y en las cartas informales.

4.6 La pasiva impersonal: it is said that

Para informar de opiniones, rumores o creencias generales sin decir quién las tiene, el inglés usa verbos de opinión o de información en pasiva: say, think, believe, know, consider, expect, report, claim, estimate, suppose, rumour, understand.

La primera construcción es la pasiva impersonal: It + be + participio + that + oración. People say that he is a genius → It is said that he is a genius. They believe that the thieves escaped by car → It is believed that the thieves escaped by car. Experts expect that prices will rise → It is expected that prices will rise.

El verbo de opinión puede ir en cualquier tiempo: It was thought that the Earth was flat. It has been reported that two people were injured.

Esta estructura es muy propia de las noticias y de los textos académicos, y es un recurso excelente para un writing formal: It is widely believed that social media has changed the way we communicate. It is often argued that… Además, permite presentar una idea sin hacerla propia, algo útil para introducir argumentos que luego vamos a rebatir.

Vídeo: Impersonal passives en inglés: explicación con ejemplos y ejercicios · Inglés Para Perezosos (YouTube) · 423 mil visualizaciones

4.7 La pasiva personal: he is said to be

La segunda construcción toma como sujeto a la persona o cosa de la que se habla: sujeto + be + participio + infinitivo. It is said that he is a genius → He is said to be a genius. Es más frecuente y más elegante que la impersonal.

La forma del infinitivo depende de la relación temporal entre el verbo de opinión y la acción:

La acción es…InfinitivoEjemplo
simultáneato + baseShe is thought to be the best candidate.
en cursoto be + -ingHe is believed to be hiding in the mountains.
anteriorto have + participioThe castle is said to have been built in 1200.
anterior y en cursoto have been + -ingThey are reported to have been living abroad.
futurato + base (con expect)Prices are expected to rise.

Transformación paso a paso: People believe that the thieves escaped in a red car. 1) El sujeto será the thieves. 2) El verbo de opinión, en pasiva y en el mismo tiempo: are believed. 3) escaped es anterior a believe: to have escaped. Resultado: The thieves are believed to have escaped in a red car.

4.8 There is thought to be y otras variantes

Cuando la frase original empieza con there is / there are, la pasiva personal mantiene there como sujeto: People think that there are over 1,000 species in the area → There are thought to be over 1,000 species in the area. En pasado: There is said to have been a battle here.

Con be supposed to se expresa lo que «se supone» según la gente, a menudo con duda: This restaurant is supposed to be excellent (dicen que…). No lo confundas con el uso de obligación del tema 2: You're supposed to wear a helmet.

Algunos verbos aparecen sobre todo en la pasiva personal y no en la activa con infinitivo: be said to, be rumoured to, be reputed to. Se dice He is said to be rich, pero no *They say him to be rich.

Otros verbos de opinión forman la pasiva personal con un complemento sin infinitivo: He is considered (to be) one of the best writers of his generation. She was regarded as a hero. En las noticias: Three people are reported missing. The suspect is understood to have left the country.

4.9 La causativa: have / get something done

La causativa expresa que otra persona hace algo para nosotros, normalmente un servicio que pedimos o pagamos: have + objeto + participio. I cut my hair (me lo corto yo) frente a I had my hair cut (me lo corté en la peluquería).

Have se conjuga en todos los tiempos: We're having the kitchen painted. She has her car serviced every year. I'll have the documents sent to you. They've just had solar panels installed. Si interesa el agente, se añade con by: I had my teeth checked by a new dentist.

Get something done significa lo mismo, en un registro más informal, y a veces sugiere esfuerzo o urgencia: I need to get my phone fixed. You should get that cough looked at.

Cuidado con el orden: el objeto va entre have y el participio. I had repaired my car (past perfect: lo arreglé yo) ≠ I had my car repaired (causativa: me lo arreglaron).

En la PAU es una reescritura clásica: A mechanic is repairing my car → I am having my car repaired. Someone cleans our windows every month → We have our windows cleaned every month.

Vídeo: Causative verbs: have, get, make, let · Arnel's Everyday English (YouTube) · 1,6 millones de visualizaciones

4.10 Causativas con personas: have, get, make, let y help

Cuando mencionamos a la persona que hace la acción, cada verbo causativo lleva su propia estructura:

VerboEstructuraSignificadoEjemplo
havehave + persona + baseencargarI'll have the receptionist call you.
getget + persona + to + baseconvencerI got my sister to help me.
makemake + persona + baseobligarThe teacher made us rewrite it.
letlet + persona + basepermitirMy parents let me stay out late.
helphelp + persona + (to) + baseayudarShe helped me (to) move.

En pasiva, make recupera el to: We were made to rewrite the essay (nos obligaron). Let no tiene pasiva: se usa be allowed to: I was allowed to stay out late.

No mezcles las estructuras: *I made him to apologise → I made him apologise; *She got me help her → She got me to help her; *They let us to leave → They let us leave.

Vídeo: Causative verbs: have, get, make, let, help · English with Lucy (YouTube) · 1,3 millones de visualizaciones

4.11 Have something done para experiencias negativas

La estructura have + objeto + participio también describe algo desagradable que nos ocurrió sin que lo pidiéramos: I had my wallet stolen on the underground. She had her bag searched at the airport. They had their flight cancelled. En estos casos equivale a una pasiva: My wallet was stolen.

Con get es igual de frecuente en registro informal: He got his nose broken in a fight. I got my car scratched.

Otra estructura relacionada es need / want + -ing con sentido pasivo: The car needs washing (= needs to be washed). The walls want painting (británico, informal).

En las historias y relatos (incluidos los textos de la PAU), estas causativas ayudan a contar incidentes sin dar protagonismo al culpable: On my first day in London, I had my phone stolen and I had to get a new SIM card sent from Spain.

4.12 La pasiva en la PAU y en el writing

La pasiva aparece en la PAU de tres maneras: en los textos de comprensión (noticias, divulgación), en las reescrituras y como recurso de estilo en el writing.

OriginalReescritura
They will open the new hospital next year.The new hospital will be opened next year.
Someone has broken the window.The window has been broken.
People say that he lives in Paris.He is said to live in Paris.
They think the fire started in the kitchen.The fire is thought to have started in the kitchen.
A plumber fixed our shower.We had our shower fixed.
They made us wait for hours.We were made to wait for hours.

En el writing, la pasiva da un tono objetivo y formal: It is widely accepted that…, Measures should be taken to…, A solution must be found. Pero no abuses: un texto entero en pasiva resulta pesado. Combina activa y pasiva según qué quieras destacar.

Revisa siempre tres cosas: el tiempo de be, el participio (irregulares: written, chosen, built, thrown) y la concordancia del sujeto (The results were published).

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Pasa a pasiva: «They are building a new stadium in the city centre.»

  1. Objeto: a new stadium. Tiempo: present continuous.
  2. is being + participio; el agente (they) no aporta nada.

Resultado: A new stadium is being built in the city centre.

Ejemplo 2. Pasa a pasiva con la persona como sujeto: «The company offered Luis a job.»

  1. Verbo con dos objetos.
  2. La persona pasa a sujeto: Luis was offered…

Resultado: Luis was offered a job (by the company).

Ejemplo 3. Reescribe: «People believe that the painting is worth millions.» → «The painting ___.»

  1. Pasiva personal con la misma época.
  2. is believed + to be.

Resultado: The painting is believed to be worth millions.

Ejemplo 4. Reescribe: «They say that the thief escaped through the roof.» → «The thief ___.»

  1. La huida es anterior a say.
  2. Infinitivo perfecto: to have escaped.

Resultado: The thief is said to have escaped through the roof.

Ejemplo 5. Reescribe con causativa: «An optician tested my eyes yesterday.»

  1. Servicio que alguien hace para mí.
  2. have + objeto + participio en past simple.

Resultado: I had my eyes tested yesterday.

Ejemplo 6. Pasa a pasiva: «The coach made the players run ten laps.»

  1. Make en pasiva recupera el to.
  2. were made + to + base.

Resultado: The players were made to run ten laps.

Errores típicos

  • Olvidar el verbo be: *The house built in 1900 → The house was built in 1900.
  • Usar la persona como sujeto con explain o suggest: *We were explained the rules → The rules were explained to us.
  • Perder la preposición: *He was laughed → He was laughed at.
  • Infinitivo incorrecto en la pasiva personal: *He is said to steal the money (en pasado) → He is said to have stolen the money.
  • Confundir el orden causativo: *I had cut my hair (en la peluquería) → I had my hair cut.
  • Poner to tras make en activa: *They made me to wait → They made me wait (pero I was made to wait).

PracticaResponde sin mirar arriba. Equivocarse aquí también enseña.

Ejercicios (32)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Pasa a pasiva: «They grow coffee in Colombia.»

    Ver solución
    Coffee is grown in Colombia.

  2. Pasa a pasiva: «Someone stole my bike yesterday.»

    Ver solución
    My bike was stolen yesterday.

  3. Pasa a pasiva: «They have cancelled the concert.»

    Ver solución
    The concert has been cancelled.

  4. Pasa a pasiva: «They will announce the results tomorrow.»

    Ver solución
    The results will be announced tomorrow.

  5. Pasa a pasiva: «They are painting the classroom.»

    Ver solución
    The classroom is being painted.

  6. Pasa a pasiva incluyendo el agente: «Cervantes wrote Don Quixote.»

    Ver solución
    Don Quixote was written by Cervantes.

  7. Completa: «The windows must ___ (clean) every week.»

    Ver solución
    be cleaned: modal + be + participio.

  8. Completa: «I hate ___ (tell) what to do.»

    Ver solución
    being told: gerundio pasivo.

  9. Completa con causativa: «I ___ my car ___ (wash) every Saturday.»

    Ver solución
    have, washed: have something done.

  10. Corrige: «The bridge was build in 1890.»

    Ver solución
    The bridge was built in 1890: participio irregular.

  11. Completa: «My parents let me ___ (go) to the party.»

    Ver solución
    go: let + base.

  12. Completa: «The meeting has been called ___.» (cancelado)

    Ver solución
    off: call off, phrasal verb en pasiva.

Nivel medio

  1. Pasa a pasiva con la persona como sujeto: «They told us that the trip was cancelled.»

    Ver solución
    We were told that the trip was cancelled.

  2. Pasa a pasiva: «They explained the problem to the students.»

    Ver solución
    The problem was explained to the students (no *The students were explained…).

  3. Pasa a pasiva: «Nobody has looked after the garden for years.»

    Ver solución
    The garden hasn't been looked after for years.

  4. Reescribe: «It is said that she speaks six languages.» → «She ___.»

    Ver solución
    She is said to speak six languages.

  5. Reescribe: «People think that the fire was caused by a cigarette.» → «The fire ___.»

    Ver solución
    The fire is thought to have been caused by a cigarette.

  6. Reescribe: «People believe that the suspect is hiding in Portugal.» → «The suspect ___.»

    Ver solución
    The suspect is believed to be hiding in Portugal.

  7. Reescribe: «Experts expect that the population will double.» → «The population ___.»

    Ver solución
    The population is expected to double.

  8. Reescribe con causativa: «A photographer is taking our wedding photos.»

    Ver solución
    We are having our wedding photos taken.

  9. Reescribe: «I persuaded my brother to lend me his car.» con get.

    Ver solución
    I got my brother to lend me his car.

  10. Pasa a pasiva: «The police made him tell the truth.»

    Ver solución
    He was made to tell the truth.

  11. Reescribe: «Someone stole my passport in Rome.» → «I had ___.»

    Ver solución
    I had my passport stolen in Rome.

  12. Completa: «She was lucky to ___ (choose) for the team last year.»

    Ver solución
    have been chosen: infinitivo pasivo perfecto.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Reescribe: «People say that there are ghosts in the castle.» → «There ___.»

    Ver solución
    There are said to be ghosts in the castle.

  2. Reescribe: «They reported that the minister had been living abroad.» → «The minister ___.»

    Ver solución
    The minister was reported to have been living abroad.

  3. Reescribe: «It is thought that the Vikings reached America first.» → «The Vikings ___.»

    Ver solución
    The Vikings are thought to have reached America first.

  4. Pasa a pasiva: «Somebody should have warned us about the storm.»

    Ver solución
    We should have been warned about the storm.

  5. Reescribe en registro formal para un ensayo: «People widely believe that technology makes life easier.»

    Ver solución
    It is widely believed that technology makes life easier / Technology is widely believed to make life easier.

  6. Completa el texto: «The new library ___ (open) last month. It ___ (design) by a local architect and ___ (expect) to attract thousands of visitors. Before that, the building ___ (use) as a factory for decades.»

    Ver solución
    was opened, was designed, is expected, had been used.

  7. Corrige los cuatro errores: «I had cut my hair yesterday at the hairdresser's. We were explained the new rules. He was made apologise. The castle is said to be built in 1300.»

    Ver solución
    I had my hair cut yesterday; The new rules were explained to us; He was made to apologise; The castle is said to have been built in 1300.

  8. Escribe un párrafo de 70 palabras tipo noticia sobre un robo con al menos cuatro pasivas, una de ellas personal (is said to / is believed to).

    Ver solución
    Modelo: A valuable painting was stolen from the city museum last night. The alarm had been switched off and no windows were broken. The thieves are believed to have entered through the roof. A security guard was found tied up in the basement. The painting is said to be worth over two million euros. The investigation is being led by the regional police.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeThe school news bulletin

El instituto lanza un boletín digital en inglés. Cada grupo redactará la noticia principal de un número especial sobre un misterio histórico de la ciudad o sobre un acontecimiento del centro, con el estilo objetivo de la prensa británica.

Pasos

  1. Elegid el tema y buscad información en fuentes fiables.
  2. Escribid un titular y una entradilla con present simple y present perfect pasivos.
  3. Redactad el cuerpo de la noticia con pasivas en distintos tiempos y al menos dos pasivas personales (is said to, is believed to).
  4. Incluid declaraciones con causativas y verbos con preposición en pasiva.
  5. Maquetad la noticia, revisad la pasiva con la lista del tema y publicadla en el boletín.

Producto final: Noticia de 200 a 250 palabras con titular, entradilla y foto.

Cómo se valora

  • Usa la pasiva en al menos cinco tiempos o formas distintas.
  • Incluye pasivas impersonales y personales correctas.
  • Emplea la causativa adecuadamente.
  • El texto tiene el tono objetivo y la estructura de una noticia.

Glosario

Active voice
Voz activa: el sujeto realiza la acción.
Passive voice
Voz pasiva: el sujeto recibe la acción (be + participio).
Agent
Quien realiza la acción en la pasiva, introducido por by.
Past participle
Participio: done, written, built.
Passive infinitive
Infinitivo pasivo: to be done, to have been done.
Passive gerund
Gerundio pasivo: being done.
Indirect object
Objeto indirecto: la persona que recibe algo.
Prepositional verb
Verbo con preposición: look after, deal with.
Get passive
Pasiva informal con get: got stolen.
Impersonal passive
It + be + participio + that: It is said that…
Personal passive
Sujeto + be + participio + infinitivo: He is said to…
Reporting verb
Verbo de opinión o información: say, believe, report.
Causative
Estructura que indica que otro hace algo por nosotros.
Have something done
Encargar un servicio: I had my hair cut.
Get someone to do
Conseguir que alguien haga algo.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Leed juntos una noticia breve en inglés y buscad las formas pasivas.
  • Hablad de los servicios que se hacen en casa: «We have the boiler checked every year».
  • Jugad a contar rumores con «He is said to…».
  • Repasad las tarjetas del tema cada noche durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Saberes básicos de Lengua Extranjera II (Inglés) de 2º de Bachillerato (RD 243/2022, BOE-A-2022-5521, bloques A. Comunicación, B. Plurilingüismo y C. Interculturalidad; en Cataluña, Decret 171/2022, Llengua Estrangera II), con la mirada puesta en la prueba de acceso a la universidad (PAU): funciones comunicativas de descripción de procesos, transmisión de información y opiniones de forma impersonal, y expresión de servicios encargados; voz pasiva en todos los tiempos, con modales, infinitivos y gerundios; pasiva de verbos con dos objetos y de verbos preposicionales; pasivas impersonales y personales con verbos de opinión; estructuras causativas (have / get something done, have / get / make / let someone do).

  • Taller de noticias: reescribir titulares en pasiva con el estilo de la prensa británica.
  • Juego de rumores: «Our teacher is said to have…» con datos inventados y divertidos.
  • Descripción de un proceso (cómo se fabrica el chocolate) con present simple pasivo.
  • Concurso de reescritura tipo PAU por parejas.

Fuentes y revisión

  • Decret 171/2022, d'ordenació dels ensenyaments del batxillerat (DOGC)

Revisado el 21 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Explicar por qué y cuándo se usa la voz pasiva en inglés y cuándo incluir el agente
  • Formar la pasiva en todos los tiempos, con modales, infinitivos y gerundios
  • Pasar a pasiva verbos con dos objetos, verbos con preposición y phrasal verbs
  • Construir las pasivas impersonales (It is said that…) y personales (He is said to…)
  • Usar la estructura causativa have / get something done y have / get / make someone do
  • Aplicar la pasiva en las reescrituras de la PAU y en textos formales sin abusar de ella

Palabras clave

be + past participle · by + agent · passive infinitive / gerund · two objects · prepositional verbs · get passive · it is said that · he is said to have · there is thought to be · have something done · get someone to do · be made to do
